links.outcome: Physician diagnostic performance with versus without AI assistance, including automation bias
links.effect: PULSE assistance enabled physicians to correct initial errors and broaden diagnostic hypotheses, but also introduced risks of automation bias; serial and concurrent workflows were explored.
links.quote: When used collaboratively, PULSE enabled physicians to correct initial errors and broaden diagnostic hypotheses, but also introduced risks of automation bias.

links.outcome: Comparison of AI diagnostic accuracy against physicians of varying expertise on same cases
links.effect: PULSE outperformed residents and junior specialists and matched senior specialists at Top@1 and Top@4.
links.quote: PULSE attained expert-competitive accuracy, outperforming residents and junior specialists while matching senior specialist performance at both Top@1 and Top@4 thresholds.

links.outcome: Automation bias when physicians use AI assistance in diagnosis
links.effect: Collaborative use introduced risks of automation bias, despite helping correct initial errors.
links.quote: When used collaboratively, PULSE enabled physicians to correct initial errors and broaden diagnostic hypotheses, but also introduced risks of automation bias.

screen.reason: Empirical study evaluating an LLM diagnostic agent (PULSE) interacting with clinicians across different collaboration workflows (serial vs concurrent) and assessing automation bias.
